executiveSummary: Checkout's p99 latency doubled to 900 ms because one loop called the pricing service once per cart item. Batching the calls, a 30-second cache, and a lint rule took p99 to 120 ms and lifted conversion 3.1%.

slides.slideTitle: How we cut p99 latency from 900 ms to 120 ms
slides.subtitle: Checkout service · Platform Engineering · 20 minutes
slides.speakerNotes:
- I'm going to show you one fix that took p99 from 900 ms to 120 ms.
- The fix was twelve lines. Finding it took six weeks.

slides.slideTitle: Checkout's p99 was 900 ms, and it was getting worse
slides.subtitle: p99 latency, ms, by month
keyBullets: p99 doubled in six months while p50 stayed flat
slides.speakerNotes: - p50 is flat. p99 doubled. That gap is the whole story.

slides.slideTitle: Every slow request went through the same three services
keyBullets: Client: Web checkout
Client: Mobile app
Service: API gateway
Service: Checkout service
Service: Pricing service
Data: Postgres
slides.speakerNotes:
- The slow path: gateway, checkout, pricing, Postgres.
- Pricing was the suspect from day one. It was innocent.

slides.slideTitle: The traces showed one request making 40 pricing calls
keyBullets: pricing calls in a single slow checkout
slides.speakerNotes:
- One checkout, forty round trips to pricing.
- A cart with forty items made forty calls.
slides.intent: Make the audience see the cause

slides.slideTitle: The loop called pricing once per item
slides.subtitle: checkout/price.go
keyBullets: Before: for _, item := range cart.Items { p, err := pricing.Get(ctx, item.SKU) }
After: prices, err := pricing.GetMany(ctx, cart.SKUs())
slides.speakerNotes:
- Before: N calls. After: one.
- The pricing service already had a batch endpoint. Nobody used it.
slides.intent: Make engineers see how small the change was

slides.slideTitle: We shipped the fix in four steps
keyBullets: Measure: add a span around every pricing call
Batch: call GetMany once per cart
Cache: keep prices 30 seconds per SKU
Guard: fail the build if a loop calls a remote service
slides.speakerNotes: - The last step matters most. It stops this coming back.

slides.slideTitle: The lint rule that keeps it fixed
slides.subtitle: tools/lint/remote_in_loop.go
keyBullets: if call.IsRemote() && inLoop(call) { report(call, "remote call inside a loop") }
It runs in CI on every pull request
It found 11 more loops on its first run
slides.speakerNotes: - Eleven more loops. Three of them were in checkout.
slides.intent: Show how to keep it fixed

slides.slideTitle: p99 fell from 900 ms to 120 ms
slides.subtitle: p99 latency, ms
keyBullets: An 87% cut, from a twelve-line change
slides.speakerNotes: - Batching got us to 210. The cache got us to 120.

keyBullets: 120 ms: p99 checkout latency
+3.1%: checkout conversion
−38%: pricing service CPU
0: pages since the fix
slides.speakerNotes: - Conversion is up 3.1%. That's the number the business cares about.
slides.intent: Tie the fix to the business

slides.slideTitle: Three lessons for your own services
keyBullets: Watch p99, not p50: the mean hides the tail
Trace one slow request end to end before you guess
Make the fix a rule, so the next person cannot undo it
slides.speakerNotes: - If you take one thing away: trace one slow request before you guess.
slides.intent: Give engineers something to use tomorrow

keyBullets: Why not cache everything?
How do you find loops that call a service?
What did the cache cost in staleness?
